questions.question: A group of men committed to completing a task in 20 days. The work was completed in 40 days because 5 workers did not come for work. Determine the number of men who originally agreed to do the work.
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

A group of men committed to a task in 20 days 

5 workers did not come for work 

Work was completed in 40 days 

**FORMULA USED:**

Efficiency = Total unit/No. of days 

**CALCULATION:**

Let us take the number of men originally agreed be x and days = 20

After when 5 men did not come for work , then men present = ( x - 5) and days = 40

Now, m₁ × d₁ = m₂ × d₂ 

⇒ x × 20 = ( x - 5) × 40 

⇒ 20x = 40x - 200 

⇒ 20x = 200 

⇒ x = 10 

**Hence, number of men originally agreed to do the work is 10.**

questions.question: 24 men can complete a work in 15 days. How many men are needed to complete the same work in 10 days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

24 men can complete a work in 15 days

**Concept Used:**

(M1 × D1) = (M2 × D2)

M1 = Initial men, D1 = Initial day, M₂ = Final men, D₂ = Final day

**Calculation:**

⇒ (M₁ × D₁) = (M₂ × D₂)

⇒ 24 × 15 = M2 × 10

⇒ M2 = 36

**Therefore, 36 men will complete the same work in 10 days.**

questions.question: At a construction site, Raju can paint a wall in 36 hours, while Angad can do the same work in 18 hours. Sumit can paint the same wall in 24 hours. In how much time can they paint the wall if they all work together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 36, 18, and 24 = 72 units.

Combined efficiency = (72 ÷ 36) + (72 ÷ 18) + (72 ÷ 24).

Combined efficiency = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 units/hour.

Time taken together = Total Work ÷ Combined efficiency = 72 ÷ 9 = 8 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept is identical to Time & Work. Inlet pipes do positive work (filling), while outlet pipes do negative work (emptying). Net efficiency determines the total time to fill or empty the tank.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the direct ratio of the total work done by each individual. If multiple people work together for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When workers operate on alternate days, you must calculate the total work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 workers). Multiply the cycle to get as close to the total work as possible before calculating the remaining days individually.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 10 days, while A and B together can complete it in 2(1)/(2) days. How long will B alone take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can complete the work in 2(1)/(2) days.

A alone can complete the work in 10 days.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Work done by A each day = (1)/(10)

⇒ According to the question,

⇒ (1)/(10)+(1)/(B)=(2)/(5)

⇒ (1)/(B)=(2)/(5)-(1)/(10)

⇒ (1)/(B)=(4-1)/(10) = (3)/(10)

⇒ B = (10)/(3)

**Therefore, B alone will take (10)/(3) days to complete the work.**

questions.question: If 24 people can build 90 identical walls in 25 days, then how many more days will 27 people require to build 162 such walls?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

24 people can build 90 walls in 25 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work = Number of People × Number of Days

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be W.

W = 90 walls

Work per person per day = W / (Number of People × Number of Days)

Work per person per day = 90 / (24 × 25)

Work per person per day = 90 / 600

Work per person per day = 0.15 walls

Total work to build 162 walls = 162 walls

Let the number of days required by 27 people be D.

Work per day by 27 people = 27 × 0.15

Work per day by 27 people = 4.05 walls

Total work = Work per day × Number of Days

162 = 4.05 × D

⇒ D = 162 / 4.05

⇒ D = 40

Original days = 25 days

Additional days required = 40 - 25

⇒ Additional days required = 15

**The number of additional days required is 15.**

questions.question: 18 workers can complete a piece of work in 96 days. They start working together and after 26 days 10 more workers join them. In how many days in all will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

18 workers can complete a piece of work in 96 days.

They start working together and after 26 days 10 more workers join them.

**Formula Used:**

Work done = Number of workers × Number of days

**Calculation:**

Work done by 18 workers in 96 days = 18 × 96

Total work = 1728 units

Work done by 18 workers in 26 days = 18 × 26

Work done in 26 days = 468 units

Remaining work = 1728 - 468

Remaining work = 1260 units

Total workers after 26 days = 18 + 10

Total workers = 28

Number of days required by 28 workers to complete the remaining work:

⇒ 28 × Days = 1260

⇒ Days = 1260 / 28

⇒ Days = 45

Total days to complete the work = 26 + 45

Total days = 71

**The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: There are 3 taps, A, B and C, in a tank. These can fill the tank in 10 h, 20 h and 25 h, respectively. At first, all three taps are opened simultaneously. After 2 h, tap C is closed and tap A and B keep running. After 4 h, tap B is also closed. The remaining tank is filled by tap A alone. Find the percentage of work done by tap A itself.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by tap A = 10 h

Time taken by tap B = 20 h

Time taken by tap C = 25 h

**Calculation:**

Total volume of tank filled by taps = LCM(10, 20 and 25) = 100 units

Filled by tap A in 1 hr = 10 units

Filled by tap B in 1 hr = 5 units

Filled by tap C in 1 hr = 4 units

Tap A, B and C can fill together = 10 + 5 + 4 = 19 units

After 2 hrs, tap C is closed,

Amount of tank filled = 2 × 19 = 38 units

After 4 hrs, tap B is also closed,

For 2 hours, tap A and B was open.

Units of water filled = (10 + 5) × 2 = 30 units

Amount of water filled by A alone = 100 – (30 + 38) = 32 units

Total units of water filled by tap A = 20 + 20 + 32 = 72 units

Percentage of work done by A itself = (72/100) × 100 = 72%

**∴ The correct answer is 72%.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 10 days. B can do it in 15 days. With the assistance of C they completed the work in 5 days. Find in how many days C alone can do it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a piece of work in 10 days.

B can do it in 15 days. 

With the assistance of C, they completed the work in 5 days

**Formula Used:**

Total work = Efficiency x Time taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ A can-do work = 10 days

⇒ B can do the work = 15 days

⇒ A + B + C can do the work = 5 days

For total work

⇒ Total work = LCM of (10, 15, 5) = 30

⇒ Efficiency of A = Total Work / Time taken = 30/10 = 3 unit

⇒ Efficiency of B = Total Work / Time taken = 30/15 = 2 unit

⇒ Efficiency of A + B + C= Total Work / Time taken = 30/5 = 6 unit

⇒ The efficiency of C = Efficiency of A + B + C - Efficiency of A - Efficiency of B = 6 - 3 - 2 = 1

Time taken by C to do the work alone

⇒ Time taken = Total Work/Efficiency = 30/1 = 30 days

⇒ **Hence, C can do the work alone in 30 days.**

questions.question: 8 men and 12 women finish a job in 4 days. While 6 men and 14 women in 5 days. In how many days will 20 women finish the job?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

8 men and 12 women finish a job in 4 days

6 men and 14 women in 5 days

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let 1 man's and 1 woman's 1-day work be x and y respectively

⇒ Then, 8x + 12y = (1)/(4) --------(1)

⇒ 6x + 14y = (1)/(5) --------(2)

⇒ Multiplying equation 1 by 6 and equation 2 by 8 we get,

⇒ 48x + 72y = (3)/(2) --------(3)

⇒ 48x + 112y = (8)/(5) --------(4)

⇒ Subtracting equation 3 from 4 we get,

⇒ 40y = (1)/(10)

⇒ y = (1)/(400)

⇒ Thus 1 woman can finish it in 400 days

⇒ So time taken by 20 women to finish the work = (400)/(20) = 20 days

**Therefore, 20 women can finish the job in 20 days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

⇒ 32M + 48W = 30M + 70W

⇒ 2M = 22W

⇒ (M)/(W) = (11)/(1) [ efficiency of M : W = 11 : 1 ]

So, the total work done is,

⇒ [ (8 × 11) + (12 × 1) ] × 4

⇒ [ 88 + 12 ] × 4

⇒ 400

So, 20 women do this work in (400)/(20) = 20 days

questions.question: A and B can complete a work in 36 days and 45 days respectively. They worked together for 2 days and then A left the work. In how many days will B complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A can do the work = 36 days

B can do the same work = 45 days

They work for 2 days and then A left 

Formula Used:

Total work = Efficiency x Time taken

Calculation:

⇒ A can do the work = 36 days

⇒ B can do the same work = 45 days

For total work, we have to take LCM of 36 and 45

⇒ Total work = LCM of 36 and 45 = 180

⇒ Efficiency of A = Total work / Efficiency = 180/36 = 5 unit

⇒ Efficiency of B = Total work / Efficiency = 180/45 = 4 unit

⇒ The efficiency of Both = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B = 4 + 5 = 9 unit

As they work for 2 days

⇒ Work completed in 2 days = 9 x 2 = 18 unit work

⇒ Remaining work = 180 - 18 = 162 unit work

Now, A left, and the remaining work is completed by B

⇒ Time was taken by B to complete the work = Total work / Efficiency = 162 / 4 = 40.5 days

⇒ **Hence, The work done by B after A left is 40.5 days**

questions.question: P and Q can do a piece of work in 14 days. Q and R together can do it in 21 days. If P is twice as good a workman as R, then in how many days Q alone can do the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of days P and Q take to do a piece of work = 14 days

Number of days Q and R take to do a work = 21 days

P is twice as good as workman as R

**Calculation:**

Let P, Q and R can do the work in x, y, and z days respectively.

Amount of work done by P, Q, and R in 1 day is 1/x, 1/y, and 1/z respectively.

According to the question,

⇒ (1)/(x)+(1)/(y)=(1)/(14) (1)

⇒ (1)/(y)+(1)/(z)=(1)/(21) (2)

⇒ As per the condition given, (1)/(x)=(2)/(z)

Putting the value in (1), and subtracting (2) from (1), we get

⇒ (2)/(z)+(1)/(y)-(1)/(z)-(1)/(y)=(1)/(14)-(1)/(21)

⇒ (1)/(z)=(3-2)/(42)=(1)/(42)

⇒ z = 42 days

Putting the value of z in equation (2), we get

⇒ (1)/(y)=(1)/(21)-(1)/(42)

⇒ (1)/(y)=(2-1)/(42)=(1)/(42)

⇒ y = 42 days

**Therefore, number of days in which Q alone can finish the work is 42 days.**

questions.question: A can do a work in 20 days and B in 30 days. If they work on it together for 2 days, then what is the fraction of the work that is left?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a work in 20 days.

B can do a work in 30 days.

They work together for 2 days.

**Concept Used:**

When two or more individuals work together, their combined work rate is the sum of their individual work rates.

**Formula Used:**

Work rate of A = 1/20 work/day

Work rate of B = 1/30 work/day

Combined work rate = (1/20 + 1/30) work/day

Fraction of work done = Combined work rate × Number of days they work together

Fraction of work left = 1 - Fraction of work done

**Calculation:**

Combined work rate = 1/20 + 1/30

⇒ Combined work rate = 3/60 + 2/60

⇒ Combined work rate = 5/60 = 1/12 work/day

Fraction of work done in 2 days = (1/12) × 2

⇒ Fraction of work done = 1/6

Fraction of work left = 1 - 1/6

⇒ Fraction of work left = 6/6 - 1/6

⇒ Fraction of work left = 5/6

**∴ The fraction of the work that is left is 5/6.**

questions.question: Ankita can write a manuscript in 20 days. Ankita, along her friend Somya, can write the manuscript in 12 days. In how many days can Somya alone write the manuscript?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ankita(A) can write a manuscript in = 20 days

Ankita(A) + Somya(S) can write the manuscript in = 12 days

**Solution:**

(1)/(20) + (1)/(S) = (1)/(12)

(1)/(S) = (1)/(12) - (1)/(20)

S = (240)/(8) = 30

Somya alone can write the manuscript in 30 days.

**Hence, the correct answer is 30.**
